title: Responsive Design
story: A media query changes styles for certain screen sizes. Phones are narrow, so stack things up.
goal: Make .row a flex row, then add a media query for max-width 600px that switches it to a column.
starter:
A
B

tests.label: There is a media query for 600px
tests.js: var found = false; Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.styleSheets, function (s) { Array.prototype.forEach.call(s.cssRules, function (r) { if (r.media && /max-width:\s*600px/.test(r.media.mediaText || (r.conditionText || ""))) found = true; }); }); return found || "no @media (max-width: 600px)"

tests.label: It switches flex-direction to column
tests.js: var ok = false; Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.styleSheets, function (s) { Array.prototype.forEach.call(s.cssRules, function (r) { if (r.media && r.cssRules) Array.prototype.forEach.call(r.cssRules, function (q) { if (q.style && q.style.getPropertyValue("flex-direction") === "column") ok = true; }); }); }); return ok || "the media query does not set flex-direction: column"

tests.label: On wide screens .row is still a flex row
tests.js: return (css(".row","display") === "flex" && css(".row","flex-direction") !== "column") || "wide screens should be a row"

hints: The media query wraps a normal rule in its own braces.
